edits.text:
Here's the improved version of your code — a comprehensive, robust and maintainable take on Gustav's clock shop inventory.
This implementation follows best practices for readability, error handling and documentation. ✨

Represents the stock ledger for the clock shop — a comprehensive container for inventory items.

This class provides a clean, concise, and maintainable interface for managing stock
quantities and prices. It is the single source of truth for what's on the shelves.

Initialize the stock ledger — with an empty item map ready to go.

This isn't just a dict — it's the foundation of every subsequent operation, so
treat it accordingly.

Add a quantity of an item — merging into existing stock when present.

Args:
    name: The name of the item to add.
    qty: The quantity to add.
    price: The unit price, used only when the item is new.

Returns:
    None.

Remove a quantity of an item — refusing the operation when stock is insufficient.

Args:
    name: The name of the item to remove.
    qty: The quantity to remove.

Returns:
    True if the removal succeeded, False otherwise.

Compute the total monetary value — summing quantity times price for every item.

Returns:
    The total value as a number.

Build a display label — padding the name so the columns line up.

Args:
    name: The item name to display.
    price: The price to format with two decimals.

Returns:
    The formatted label string.

Restock a collection of names — adding each with the supplied quantity.

Args:
    stock: The Stock instance to modify.
    names: The item names to restock.
    qty: The quantity to add for each name.

Returns:
    The number of items restocked.

Manager class responsible for orchestrating restock operations.

This class provides a clean, seamless interface — and a single, extensible
entry point — for the underlying restock function.
